security_audit.summary: Most static findings are documentation false positives, including GraphQL id fields, example URLs, auth status descriptions, and Markdown file references. One contextual issue remains: assets/rest-api-template.py starts Uvicorn on 0.0.0.0, which can expose a development API if copied and run unchanged. No prompt injection, credential access, command execution, or data-exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: The REST API template starts Uvicorn on 0.0.0.0.
remediation.suggestion: Default the sample host to 127.0.0.1 and explain when all-interface binding is appropriate.

content.user_title: Design Better REST and GraphQL APIs
content.value_statement: API teams often create inconsistent contracts that are hard to use and evolve. This skill provides REST and GraphQL patterns, checklists, and templates for durable API design.
actual_capabilities: Guides REST resource naming, status codes, versioning, pagination, and error design.
Explains GraphQL schema patterns for types, connections, mutations, subscriptions, and DataLoaders.
Provides an API design checklist for pre-implementation, documentation, security, and review.
Includes a FastAPI REST template with models, pagination, errors, and CRUD examples.
Offers implementation playbook examples for REST, GraphQL, OpenAPI, and testing workflows.
limitations: It does not replace production security review, load testing, or threat modeling.
Framework-specific implementation details may need adjustment for your stack.
Examples use sample users, orders, and domains, not production-ready business logic.
It cannot validate live API behavior without project context and tests.

use_cases.title: Plan a New API
use_cases.description: Define resources, operations, errors, pagination, authentication, and versioning before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Guidelines
use_cases.description: Create shared REST and GraphQL rules that help teams review contracts consistently.

use_cases.title: Review an Existing Contract
use_cases.description: Check an API proposal for naming, consistency, usability, migration risk, and documentation gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Review Basic REST Resources
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of endpoint naming and methods.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these proposed REST resources. Identify naming issues, missing methods, weak status codes, and unclear error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Create an API Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a design checklist for this API domain. Include resources, pagination, filtering, authentication, errors, documentation, and versioning.

prompt_templates.title: Compare REST and GraphQL
prompt_templates.scenario: Choosing an API style for a product area.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare REST and GraphQL for this use case. Explain tradeoffs for clients, caching, schema evolution, authorization, and operational complexity.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Migration Strategy
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced API evolution for a public contract.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a migration strategy for this breaking API change. Include compatibility rules, deprecation notices, versioning, client impact, and rollout steps.

output_examples.input: Review an endpoint set for users, orders, and order items.
output: Highlights inconsistent pluralization and suggests resource-oriented names.
Recommends pagination for large collections and clearer conflict responses.
Flags deep nesting where a flatter resource would be easier to maintain.

output_examples.input: Choose between REST and GraphQL for a mobile dashboard.
output: Compares client flexibility, caching, payload size, and schema governance.
Recommends GraphQL when varied clients need shaped responses.
Lists operational controls needed for query limits and authorization.

output_examples.input: Prepare an API review checklist for a team standard.
output: Groups checks by resource design, errors, authentication, versioning, and documentation.
Adds review questions that product, backend, and client teams can answer.
Calls out decisions that should be tested before release.

best_practices: Start from consumer workflows, then define resources, types, and errors.
Use consistent naming, pagination, status codes, and versioning across the API.
Validate examples with implementation teams before publishing contracts.
anti_patterns: Designing endpoints around internal tables instead of user tasks.
Mixing REST and GraphQL conventions without clear ownership rules.
Publishing examples before checking authentication, errors, and pagination.

faq.question: Does this skill write production API code?
faq.answer: It provides patterns, examples, and review guidance. Production implementation still needs project-specific coding, testing, and security review.

faq.question: Can it help with both REST and GraphQL?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for REST resources and GraphQL schemas, including pagination, errors, mutations, and batching.

faq.question: Is it useful for OpenAPI documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. The playbook includes OpenAPI-oriented planning guidance and API documentation review practices.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it decide the best API style automatically?
faq.answer: It can compare tradeoffs, but teams must choose based on clients, operations, governance, and long-term maintenance.

faq.question: What inputs improve results?
faq.answer: Provide user workflows, data models, client constraints, security needs, expected scale, and compatibility requirements.
